route: Temporary Activity visa (subclass 408), Entertainment activities stream

permit.applies: The worker applies; a temporary activities sponsor is needed if applying in Australia or staying more than 3 months, otherwise a supporter.
permit.first: A contract for the performance or work; the sponsor's or supporter's consultation with the relevant union before engaging the performer; for film or television, an Arts certificate from the Department of Communications and the Arts.

fees.what: Visa application charge, base application charge, first instalment, any applicant not in a class the Minister specifies (Migration Regulations Sch. 1 item 1237(2)(a)(vi))

processing.note: Home Affairs' global processing times for subclass 408, Entertainment Activities stream: 90% of applications decided in 47 days, 75% in 36, 50% in 23 (applications decided to 31 August 2026, updated 29 September 2026).

permit.union: You must consult one or more Australian unions before the applicant submits their application under one of the following entertainment categories (film or television performers among them); directors: the Australian Directors Guild (ADG); musicians and conductors: the Musicians Union; all other applications: the Media Entertainment and Arts Alliance (MEAA).
permit.eligibility: You must have a contract for your performance or work in Australia

sources.title: Department of Home Affairs (Australia), Temporary Activity visa (subclass 408): Entertainment activities
sources.said: Stay in Australia for up to 2 years with members of the family unit … You can't stay in Australia longer by extending this visa … Applicants for this visa need a sponsor who is a temporary activities sponsor if they: apply in Australia, or apply outside Australia and intend to stay for more than 3 months … You must have a contract for your performance or work in Australia … You must consult one or more Australian unions before the applicant submits their application under one of the following entertainment categories: performing in a film or television production subsidised by government … Directors You must consult the Australian Directors Guild (ADG) for applications for foreign screen directors in film, television and digital media … All other applications You must consult the Media Entertainment and Arts Alliance (MEAA) … If the applicant is performing in a film or television production, you must provide a certificate from the Department of Communications and the Arts … For an indication of processing times for this visa, use the visa processing time guide tool
